title: Chevrolet El Camino Engines (1959–1987)
description: Every factory engine in the Chevrolet El Camino by year: the 1959–60 full-size pickup, the SS 396 and 454 LS6 of the Chevelle years, and 1980s V6s and V8s.
intro: The El Camino was Chevrolet's car-based pickup: a full-size model in 1959–1960, then built on the Chevelle and later the Malibu platform from 1964 to 1987. It shared those cars' engines, including the SS 396 and 454.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first El Camino was based on the full-size Chevrolet, with the 235 six, the 283 and the 348 W-series V8.
The Chevelle-based El Camino offered sixes, the 283 and 327, and from 1966 the 396.
The El Camino SS shared the Chevelle SS engines, including the 1970 LS6 454. Ratings are gross through 1971 and SAE net from 1972.
The Colonnade El Camino carried SAE net ratings, from the 250 six to the 454.
The downsized El Camino used V6s, the 267, 305 and 350, the Oldsmobile-built 5.7 diesel, and from 1985 the 4.3 V6.
